shipped.title_o: Revisiting the Investment Theory of Creativity
shipped.outcome_quote: The present data not only confirmed the theory-practice and gender discrepancies previously found among mainland Chinese university students

blind_target.authors: Zhang, L. F., & Sternberg, R. J.
blind_target.title: Revisiting the investment theory of creativity.
blind_target.evidence_quote: Equally importantly, this study was to establish if the aforementioned two types of discrepancies found in Zhang and Sternberg’s (2011a) work can be replicated in this study.
blind_target.outcome_quote: In Zhang and Sternberg’s study, the mainland research participants rated intellectual styles as the most important resource for crea- tivity in their explicit evaluation of the six resources, while they indicated that intel- lectual styles would be the second most important resource when they evaluated the hypothetical cases. However, in the present study, whereas the Hong Kong partici- pants’ratings of boys were consistent with those in Zhang and Sternberg’s study, their ratings of girls were not.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Authors confirm the intelligence discrepancy and gender gap, but explicitly contrast the girls’ intellectual-style ratings with the original. Abstract confirms particular gaps rather than providing an overriding overall replication verdict. The measure citation 2011b is an unpublished test, not the target 2011a finding.

shipped.title_o: Promoting Interest and Performance in High School Science Classes
shipped.outcome_quote: increased both interest and performance of low-performing students

blind_target.authors: Hulleman, C. S., & Harackiewicz, J. M.
blind_target.title: Promoting interest and performance in high school science classes.
blind_target.evidence_quote: Although the research generated by the expectancy-value framework has been largely correlational (Wigfield & Cambria, 2010), recent classroom studies reveal that interventions designed to enhance perceptions of value can increase both interest and course perfor- mance (e.g., Hulleman & Harackiewicz, 2009; Hulleman, Godes, Hendricks, & Harackiewicz, 2010). The research presented herein replicates and extends this prior work by further investigating a theory-based intervention designed to enhance student motivation and performance.
blind_target.outcome_quote: The results of Study 2 partially replicated prior research dem- onstrating that a theoretically guided intervention based on the expectancy-value framework could enhance student learning out- comes (Hulleman & Harackiewicz, 2009; Hulleman et al., 2010).
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly give a partial-replication verdict over both cited prior intervention papers; interest/performance benefits coexist with an unexpected mechanism.

shipped.title_o: Modulating the neural bases of persuasion: why/how, gain/loss, and users/non-users
shipped.outcome_quote: Consistent with prior fMRI work, activity in mPFC was significantly associated with message-consistent behavior change, above and beyond self-reported intentions.

blind_target.authors: Vezich I.S., Katzman P.L., Ames D.L., Falk E.B., Lieberman M.D.
blind_target.title: Modulating the neural bases of persuasion: why/how, gain/loss, and users/non-users
blind_target.evidence_quote: Specifically, we replicated the procedure of Vezich et al. (2017) . In this work, participants viewed persuasive paragraphs about using sunscreen everyday, and then were surveyed about their intentions for future sunscreen use. A week later, they were re-contacted about their sunscreen use following the imaging session. They found a significant relationship between activity in the mPFC during message exposure and later sunscreen use after the scan.
blind_target.outcome_quote: However, we did not find any activation differences between different kinds of persuasive messages. This is in contrast with the original study, which identified greater neural activation on an average for gain over fact and loss messages. In addition, the successful replication results above are the result of using a different neural activity parameter than in Vezich et al. (all persuasive messages over baseline, vs gain > fact and gain > loss). The original contrasts, gain > loss and gain > fact, did not replicate the user/non-user interaction and were weaker predictors of mPFC activity for the whole group than the baseline contrast was.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Authors replicate the activity-behavior relationship and user/non-user difference with a changed contrast, while explicitly contrasting the absent message-framing activation differences and failed original contrasts. Affirmation of a particular effect is not an overall verdict overriding these contrasts.

shipped.title_o: Multiple symbolic representations: The combination of formula and text supports problem solving in the mathematical field of propositional logic
shipped.outcome_quote: In accordance with previous research, performance was superior in conditions providing MERs compared to single-representation conditions.

blind_target.authors: Ott, N., Brünken, R., Vogel, M., & Malone, S.
blind_target.title: Multiple symbolic representations: The combination of formula and text supports problem solving in the mathematical field of propositional logic.
blind_target.evidence_quote: The main objective of the present research was to conduct a conceptual replication study (Earp & Trafimow, 2015) of Ott et al. (2018) in order to confirm the newly established homogeneous multimedia effect of multiple symbolic representations, and beyond that, to extend Ott et al.'s investigation about heterogeneous multimedia effects by using functionally equivalent graphics.
blind_target.outcome_quote:
Regarding the particular representations within MERs, the current study revealed that the text-based representation of linear systems of equations was inferior to the other representations for problem solving, whereas the graphical representation proved to be most beneficial. These findings do not correspond to Ott et al.'s (2018) assumption of a reference function for the representation text in MERs.
Regarding the distinct hypotheses, the current study provides confirming as well as contradicting evidence.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The authors confirm the performance benefit and gaze transitions, while explicitly contradicting the original text-as-reference finding. Opening confirmation concerns particular effects and does not override the explicit contrasting findings. Both original experiments are combined into a single-paper target.
